summary: Alexander von Rospatt works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig (1995), Vienna (2001), and UC Berkeley (2011–2026).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tartu, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel. He served at Saint Petersburg State University (1909), Peking University (1918–1929), and directed the Sino-Indian Institute (~1927–1937).

Alexandra David-Néel was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and under Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

Alexandra van der Geer specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He taught at Lycée Charlemagne (~1826–1838), served as inspector at the Académie de Paris (~1838–1854), and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He spent his career at Oxford, serving as Lecturer in Sanskrit (~1977–1992) and Professor (~1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner. From 1968, he held professorial posts at George Washington University, becoming Columbian Professor in 1981.
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfonsa Ferrari worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed postgraduate research at Sapienza University of Rome, studying under Giuseppe Tucci, Carlo Formichi, Theodor Bloch, Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou. She taught Sanskrit at Rome in 1952.

Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He taught at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1970–1986), and was Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).
Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, where he studied under John Peile (~1879–1883).

Alfred Cooper Woolner specialized in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford, he served as Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1928), Registrar and Principal at the University of the Punjab (1903), and Vice Chancellor there (1928–1936).

Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901) and the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926).

Alfred Edward Housman was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, Bromsgrove School, and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881), later holding a post at University College London (~1892–1911).

Alfred Ernout was a linguist who held posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1973), the University of Paris (~1927–1944), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

Alfred Forke was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), Berlin (~1914–1923), and the University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, he directed the EFEO (1905), founded the DAFA (1922), and held professorships at the University of Paris (1907, 1929–1936).

Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach and at the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex (~1971–1974), Australian National University (1974–1979), and the London School of Economics (1979).

Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He served as professor at the University of Breslau from 1883 to 1902.

Alfred Körte specialized in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890) and held posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig (~1917–1934).
